Both are already linked to 331 common concepts, including mathematical foundation, finite sample performance and gamma distribution, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses mathematical foundation as a bridge: first, review how maximum likelihood estimation and quantile are each currently treated through mathematical foundation; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.

We propose a study that uses long term dependency as a bridge: first, review how risk assessment and stock price prediction are each currently treated through long term dependency; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
